title: P-256 sigma rho with explicitly counted main-phase wide control

claims.statement: For uniform full-size P-256 Q=[x]P, the cold classical algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed H1, M1/L-ori conditional fresh-exposure and H3 pricing premises. Total charged work is at most 2^127.093650 units at C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions/unit. The complete inherited walk uses A=2^24, K=2^32, theta=2^-60, tau=0.4943186 and residual Markov factor 420000. All preprocessing, failures, restarts, table initialization, lookup, transfers, replay, verification and output are included. A specified 128-bit main-phase control wrapper costs at most 256 instructions per full batch round; finishing rounds retain 1024. The measured batch kernel is unchanged. Common work uses the measured plain round, derived anchor excess and this explicit phase-specific control charge. The table uses (key>>84) mod C and a separately charged bias debit; its eager zeroing is included. Peak memory is below 2^77 bytes, preprocessing at most 2^62.848092 units, and nonuniform advice zero. The conditional success margin remains at least 1e-5 above 0.39. Production probability and universal instruction bounds remain heuristic premises, not certifications. Measurements and finite experiments retain their original scope and attribution.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the revised full production cost ledger and order certificate, then run the inherited complete reduced-order procedure at tau=0.4943, the production value on its 0.0001 grid, retaining failures and replay checks. The two results have distinct scopes; neither establishes production mixing.
